current.text: He re-signed with Minnesota on a minimum contract and adds guard depth.
He is in Minnesota's 10-man rotation as a bench scoring option at about 15 minutes per game.
He is a risky pick. Experts call him a roll of the dice, and a consistent role is hard for him to find.
He was solid enough when he had to start, so he can fill in if a starting guard misses time.
Minnesota's bench is thin, with little scoring punch and no ball handlers in the bench unit.
Minnesota plays a smaller, guard-heavy lineup after trading Julius Randle and Naz Reid for LaMelo Ball.
With a March 28 end, Minnesota's playoff schedule goes 4, 2, 4 games, so the semifinal week has only two games.
Minnesota has the league minimum of 13 back-to-backs.
Minnesota is expected to be a winning team (Ben predicts 53 wins) and should not rest players to tank.

durable.text: He is a bench scorer who can put up numbers when he gets minutes.

note: At rank 236 on Yahoo and 283 on ESPN, both with 0 USD value, he falls well outside the 144 players drafted in our league, so do not spend on him in the auction. Projections of about 8 points and 1.5 threes in about 16 minutes give no category edge. He only matters if an injury to a Minnesota guard pushes him into a bigger role. His two-game semifinal week also hurts his playoff use, so treat him as a short-term waiver pickup only.
